timecoded_text_to_speech.text: The technology versus humanity is really a collection of thoughts that I have about the
future of how technology is impacting people.
And if we look around ourselves, we can see that technology is becoming more powerful
every single day and what used to be science fiction is becoming science fact.
And much of that is very good because we can solve global problems like climate change
and energy and maybe cancer and diseases.
At the same time technology is changing us as people, our behaviour, our biology, our
thinking, we outsource things to technology.
And then all of a sudden technology in this exponential curve becomes extremely powerful
in the sense that we may eventually kind of lose control of what exactly it does.
And the title of technology versus humanity is really meant as a provocation.
It is not meant as a prediction.
I really think that we can sit on top of technology and be very happy with it.
But we're going to have to do something about making that balance right now and finding
something that I call digital ethics, finding a way forward with technology not being
run by technology as the bottom line of the book is really kind of embraced technology
but don't become it.
We're not going to stand here and say that in 10 years a robot will take over the world.
This is up to us to define the future of what we make it.
So it's very important to realise that technology, humanity, the topic is not technology wanting
to take over humanity yet.
We are actually creating all of these things.
We are in charge of what technology will do in the future and the decisions are being
made today, the moral, financial, economic decisions are made today and they will impact
the lives of our children.
So many ways you could say that maybe we are the last generation of humans that are not
altered by technology.
And that is a very, very big thing.
So we really have to think about what it means, what the future has taken us and how we
get in this exponential scale.
We're here now but we're going to be here in five or seven years then.
What does it mean and how do we define who we are and what technology is?

youtube_description:
This is the first episode of my new video series titled 'conversations with Gerd' see www.conversationswithgerd.com. These are short films with interviews on key topics such as technology vs humanity, digital transformation, the future of the internet, exponential change, artificial intelligence, the future of work and much more.  Produced and directed by Jean Francois Cardella, TFA Studios see http://www.futuristgerd.com/film-studio/.

This first episode is about my new book 'Technology vs Humanity' - the coming clash of man and machines (released Sept 8 2016) -  see www.techvshuman.com for more details and order details, or order direct via http://fastfuturepublishing.com/main/shop/tech-vs-human/
or gerd.io/TVHKindle

About the book: are you ready for the greatest changes in recent human history? Futurism meets humanism in Gerd Leonhard’s ground-breaking new work of critical observation, discussing the multiple Megashifts that will radically alter not just our society and economy but our values and our biology. Wherever you stand on the scale between techno mania and nostalgia for a lost world, this is a book to challenge, provoke, warn and inspire.

If you enjoy my videos and talks, please take a look at my new book “Technology vs Humanity” http://www.techvshuman.com or buy it via Amazon http://gerd.fm/globalTVHamazon
